groups.g: Agriculture and food — one line each

items.d: **A2** = paid-out costs; **A2+FL** = paid-out costs plus imputed family labour (the current MSP basis, at cost plus 50%); **C2** = comprehensive cost including imputed rent on owned land and interest on owned capital — the **Swaminathan Commission's** recommended basis and the farmers' demand.

**Buffer stock** norms are fixed quarterly for price stabilisation and PDS; the **strategic reserve** is additional, for emergencies. Actual stocks have run far above both — carrying cost, storage loss and the fiscal burden of the food subsidy are the consequences.

States procure, store and distribute on the Centre's behalf, which cuts transport cost and widens the crops procured. Odisha and Chhattisgarh are the successful adopters — the reform the Shanta Kumar Committee wanted generalised.

Leakage in the PDS fell sharply after **Aadhaar seeding, ePoS and One Nation One Ration Card** — from over 40% in earlier estimates to a much lower level, though estimates vary by method. Cite the mechanism (end-to-end computerisation) rather than a contested single figure.

**ZBNF (Subhash Palekar)** — four wheels: Jeevamrit, Beejamrit, Achhadana (mulching) and Whapasa (soil moisture). Scaled in **Andhra Pradesh's Community-Managed Natural Farming**; the **National Mission on Natural Farming (₹2,481 crore)** targets 1 crore farmers. Caution to state for balance: yield effects are contested and Sri Lanka's abrupt 2021 switch failed.

Crop + livestock + fishery + agroforestry on the same holding, which raises income stability. Justification: **allied sectors now contribute ~40% of agricultural GVA and are growing faster than crops** — the fastest route to the Dalwai Committee's income goal.

India was the **first country with a National Agroforestry Policy (2014)**; bamboo was **removed from the definition of 'tree' in the Indian Forest Act in 2017**, freeing farmers to harvest and transport it from non-forest land — the classic example of a legal reclassification unlocking a livelihood.

**PPVFR Act, 2001** — India's *sui generis* alternative to UPOV, uniquely recognising **farmers' rights** to save, use, exchange and sell seed. **GEAC** clears GM releases: **Bt cotton (2002) is the only GM crop commercially approved**; Bt brinjal is under moratorium (2010) and **GM mustard (DMH-11)** approval is sub judice.

A new **Ministry of Cooperation (2021)**; the **97th Amendment** made cooperatives a fundamental right under Art. 19(1)(c) with **Art. 43B**, though Part IXB was struck down for state cooperatives in 2021. Instruments: **2 lakh new multipurpose PACS**, the world's largest decentralised grain storage plan, and three national-level cooperative societies for exports, seeds and organics.

India's farm power availability is ~2.5 kW/ha against a target of 4; **Custom Hiring Centres** address the small-holding constraint. **Namo Drone Didi** provides drones to 15,000 SHGs — mechanisation delivered as a service rather than as an asset, the right model for a 1.08 ha average holding.

groups.g: Environment and infrastructure — one line each

items.d: **Screening → scoping (ToR) → baseline study → public consultation → appraisal → clearance → monitoring**, under the **EIA Notification 2006**. Category A projects are cleared by the Centre, Category B by SEIAAs. Criticisms: post-facto clearance (held illegal in *Alembic*), weak public hearings, self-reported data, and the exemption list.

**CRZ Notification 2019** — four zones (I ecologically sensitive, II developed, III undeveloped, IV water area); relaxed the no-development zone for densely populated rural stretches. Coastal states must prepare **Coastal Zone Management Plans**; the tension is between tourism/housing pressure and mangrove and fisher-community protection.

**Wetlands (Conservation and Management) Rules, 2017** — prohibit conversion, encroachment and solid-waste dumping, with a **State Wetland Authority** and a brief document for each wetland; but the Rules **dropped the 2010 provision for a central regulatory authority**, and 'wise use' is defined by the state. India has **91 Ramsar sites**, the largest network in Asia.

**CAMPA/CAF Act, 2016** — user agencies pay for the land diverted plus the **Net Present Value** of the forest; accumulated funds exceed ₹50,000 crore. Criticism: **plantations on revenue or community land displace local rights**, and monoculture plantations do not replace a natural forest's ecosystem services.

**Solid Waste Management Rules 2016** (source segregation into three streams, user fee, spot fines), **Plastic Waste Management Rules 2016/2021** (ban on identified single-use items, **EPR from 2022**), **E-Waste Rules 2022** (EPR certificates), **Battery Waste Rules 2022**, **Construction and Demolition Rules 2016**, and **Bio-Medical Waste Rules 2016**.

**NAAQS (2009, 12 pollutants)**, the **AQI (2014, six categories from Good to Severe)**, **NCAP (2019, 131 non-attainment cities, 40% PM reduction by 2025-26)**, **GRAP** in the NCR, **BS-VI from April 2020** (skipping BS-V), and the **CAQM (statutory, 2021)** whose orders override state boards in the NCR airshed.

**$100 bn a year** promised by 2020 and delivered late; the **New Collective Quantified Goal** agreed at COP29; the **Loss and Damage Fund** operationalised at COP28; **Green Climate Fund, Adaptation Fund, GEF**; **Article 6** carbon markets; and India's **sovereign green bonds** (issued since 2023) with the green taxonomy under development.

**BOT-Toll** (traffic risk with the developer), **BOT-Annuity** (with the government), **EPC** (government funds and owns), **HAM** (40% government during construction, 60% as annuity — the model that revived highway PPP), **TOT** (monetising operating assets), and **InvITs**. The **Kelkar Committee (2015)** fixed the risk-allocation principle: **allocate each risk to the party best able to manage it**.

**NaBFID (2021)** — the development finance institution for infrastructure; **NIIF** (three funds, sovereign-anchored); **IIFCL**; **InvITs and REITs**; **municipal bonds** (Pune 2017 onwards); and **sovereign green bonds**. The gap: India needs ~$1.5 trillion of infrastructure investment this decade, most of which must be private.

**MMDR Amendment Act, 2023** — opened **lithium, cobalt and 24 other critical and deep-seated minerals** to private exploration with an exploration licence, and reserved auction of 24 critical minerals to the Centre. **National Critical Mineral Mission (₹16,300 crore)**, **KABIL** for overseas assets, and India's membership of the **Mineral Security Partnership (2023)**.
